title: Vanguard continuous-batching recommender: workload fingerprinting, safe rollout, and rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build and roll out the ‘Vanguard’ continuous-batching recommendation engine: a daemon that profiles live request traffic, scores workload fingerprints with a latency-sensitivity heuristic, generates batching parameter candidates (batch size, max wait, coalescing window, KV cache hints), and safely applies/reverts config changes via a canary + automated rollback playbook. This ticket covers design validation, a production-safe implementation of the recommender, integration with the config service and Console rollout controls, and a documented rollback/testing runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon ingests anonymized request traces and computes workload fingerprints with <5% CPU overhead on a profiling host
Heuristic produces candidate batching parameter set that reduces per-token compute cost by >=8% on at least 3 internal workload snapshots without increasing p99 latency by >5%
Apply pipeline supports staged rollout: shadow -> 1% canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback triggers
Rollback executes within 60s of trigger and restores prior config version across affected nodes
Integration tests and a smoke dashboard (Console) exist to monitor cost/latency/error signals during rollouts
Documentation and on-call runbook (Confluence) published and reviewed by SRE and Runtime owners
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — collected 48 hours of anonymized RPS traces from prod-blue cluster; verified we can extract sequence-length and client-latency distributions without PII.

2026-03-05: Prototype heuristic v0.1 implemented (entropy-weighted fingerprint + latency-sensitivity score). Benchmarked on 3 workloads; saw 6-12% cost delta with tail latency regression on one workload.
2026-03-09: Design review with Runtime and SRE. Decided to add burst-capacity windowing and KV-cache coherence threshold before canaries to avoid regressions on bursty traffic.
2026-03-11: End-to-end shadowing implemented in staging; candidate config evaluator runs in shadow and emits metrics to metrics/vanguard/*. Worked through early instrumentation gaps.
2026-03-13: Implemented first automated rollback trigger (p99 latency + error-rate spike). Preparing canary rollout plan and on-call notifications for next sprint.
design_decisions: Fingerprinting: use aggregate histograms (sequence-length, tokens-per-request, client inter-arrival) sampled at 1s resolution to keep memory footprint low
Heuristic: combine entropy-weighted workload fingerprint with a latency-sensitivity score to weight cost vs tail-latency risk
Candidate generation: discrete parameter grid with neighborhood exploration (±10–30% around current params) instead of wide random search to limit risk
Safety: enforce a ‘no-change’ rule when recent p95 latency slope > 20% or error-rate > 0.5% to avoid chasing noisy signals
Rollout model: always run candidate in shadow for 2 hours and validate with predefined statistical tests before canary
Rollback triggers: p99 latency delta > 5% absolute or error-rate increase > 0.3% in canary cohort over 5 minutes (configurable thresholds)
Apply model: config-store version pinning + per-pool staged application with health-check gating; leverage existing rollout APIs in Console
implementation_notes: Daemon written in Go to align with runtime's existing telemetry stack; uses existing metrics client and config-store SDK
Telemetry output namespaced under metrics/vanguard.{candidate,control}. Use tags: pool, model, region, fingerprint-hash
Use lightweight bloom filter to detect unseen fingerprints and avoid applying recommendations for new/unrecognized traffic patterns
Store candidate history in S3 (or internal blobstore) with metadata including seed, fingerprint-hash, measurement windows, and pre/post metrics
Make the daemon opt-in per pool via annotations to allow gradual adoption by customers using Dedicated
Expose a dry-run mode that only emits Console recommendations without applying configs
rollback_plan: Automated rollback lives in the rollout controller: when a trigger fires, the controller pins the last-known-good config (tracked by config-store versioning), rolls the canary cohort back to that version, and escalates to on-call. Manual steps: (1) run `vanguard rollback --pool <pool> --to-version <version>`; (2) if rollback fails, run emergency global revert `config-store force-pin <version>` and open incident ticket. Post-incident: capture snapshot, attach to Confluence incident page, and schedule blameless postmortem.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint encoder and heuristic scoring
Integration tests: shadowing pipeline that compares candidate vs control metrics end-to-end in staging
Chaos test: inject synthetic latency spikes during shadow and ensure heuristic blocks rollout when sensitivity threshold met
E2E canary validation in a reserved test-zone before any production rollout
Performance regression test to assert daemon CPU < 5% of profiling host and memory < 512MB
telemetry_queries: dashboards/console/vanguard-smoke: panel showing candidate vs control token-cost and p99 latency
risks: False positives from heuristic causing unnecessary rollbacks leading to oscillation
Interplay with KV cache: aggressive batching could increase cache misses and actually increase compute in some contexts
Customer workloads with adversarial traffic patterns (very bursty or extremely long sequences) may be misclassified
Operational: insufficient observability could delay detection and lengthen rollbacks
